What to know

  • mRNA vaccines deliver a transient message. The mRNA encodes an antigen; the host cell translates it, and the immune system responds. The mRNA does not enter the genome.
  • siRNA and antisense oligonucleotides reduce protein production. They bind complementary RNA and trigger degradation or block translation.
  • RT-PCR detects RNA. Reverse transcriptase converts RNA to cDNA, then PCR amplifies it; this is used for viral load and gene-expression tests.
  • Transcriptomics measures many RNAs at once. Microarrays and RNA sequencing reveal which genes are active in a tissue or disease.
  • RNA therapeutics need delivery and stability. Lipid nanoparticles, chemical modifications, and dosing strategies protect RNA and get it into the right cells.

Check

check.question: What does an mRNA vaccine directly provide to a cell?

options.text: A temporary message for making an antigen
A permanent change to the genome
A protein drug ready to use

check.explanation: The vaccine mRNA is translated into antigen protein, then degraded. It does not integrate into DNA.
